rule: Red on >= 3 days within the sustained-Red window triggers the sustained-Red / reactive-deload path
summary: No trial validates '3 Red days' as a deload trigger; HRV-guided studies react to 1-2 low days with an easy day, not a deload. Requiring 3 of 5 filters single bad nights, and the non-joint path is only a proposal, so false positives cost an approval decision rather than a lost week. A 1-week break costs some strength in trained lifters, so the number should not be lowered without data.

sources.note: Low HRV (below reference or 2-day decreasing trend) -> easy/rest that day only; no multi-day deload trigger
Consensus supports reactive deloads when fatigue accumulates, without a specific day count
1-week deload mid-programme reduced strength gains - a trigger that fires too readily has a cost
